summary: Master disaster-resilient urban planning. Learn GIS hazard mapping, Sendai Framework alignment, and resilient infrastructure design. Enroll today.
lede: Disaster-resilient urban planning combines hazard assessment with decisions intended to reduce urban vulnerability. Designed for urban planning, resilience and infrastructure professionals, the course covers practical tasks including GIS-based multi-hazard mapping, planning Blue-Green infrastructure for stormwater management, and developing risk-sensitive land-use policies and resilient building codes.
audienceIntro: This program is tailored for mid-to-senior level professionals responsible for the long-term safety and functionality of urban environments.
modules: Foundations of Urban Resilience and Global Frameworks
Spatial Risk Assessment and Hazard Mapping
Resilient Land Use and Regulatory Policy
Social and Economic Dimensions of Urban Resilience
Strategic Integration and Resilience Action Planning
prerequisites: Participants should have at least three years of experience in urban planning, civil engineering, environmental management, or disaster risk reduction. A basic understanding of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) concepts is recommended, though advanced technical proficiency is not required. No programming or coding is necessary for this course.
